question: Will any presidential candidate win outright in the first round of the Brazil election?
resolution_criteria:
Presidential elections are scheduled to be held in Brazil on October 4, 2026. A second round will be held if no candidate secures more than 50% of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any candidate wins this election in the first round. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the result of the first round of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).
research:
I'm writing up the brief now. I'm leaving out everything I found that was published after the 2026-09-26 cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- The official source is the TSE results (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br, plus the TSE's results page). The first round is on 2026-10-04, so as of 2026-09-26 there are no results for this race. I did not fetch the TSE portal, since it would have nothing to show before the vote.
- Rule (Brazilian Constitution, Art. 77): a candidate wins in the first round only with more than 50% of **valid** votes. Blank and spoiled (null) ballots are not counted as valid votes.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In the polls I could date before the cutoff, no candidate is close to 50% of valid votes. The front-runners, Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), are in the mid-30s or lower in total votes, and several minor candidates split the rest.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-07: Genial/Quaest poll (fieldwork Sept 4-7, 2,004 interviews, margin of error ±2 pts), first round in total votes: Lula 36%, Flávio Bolsonaro 29%, Augusto Cury 8%, Renan Santos (Missão) 3%, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 3%, Romeu Zema (Novo) 2%. Excluding undecided, blank and null answers, Lula would be roughly in the mid-40s of valid votes, below 50%. That share is my own rough calculation, not a figure Quaest published. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/quaest-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-36-flavio-29-e-cury-8/)
- 2026-03 (Reuters/Datafolha): Lula 46% vs Flávio 43% in a runoff simulation, a technical tie. Lula led every first-round scenario but well below a majority. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2026-01 (Quaest): Lula 35%, Flávio 26% in the first round. [Harvard TagTeam/Quaest](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content)
- I could not find a Datafolha, AtlasIntel or Quaest poll dated between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-26.

## 4. Base rates
- Brazilian presidential elections since 1989 under the two-round system: an outright first-round win happened twice in 9 elections, both by Fernando Henrique Cardoso (1994 with about 54%, 1998 with about 53%).
- Every election since then went to a runoff: 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022, so 0 of the last 6.
- 2022 is the closest recent case. Lula got 48.4% of valid votes in the first round, short of 50%, even though some final polls had shown him near or above 50% of valid votes. Polls underestimated Bolsonaro by several points. [CBC](https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6603351)
- In 2026, the clearest polling difference from 2022 is that both front-runners are well below 50% of valid votes, with Augusto Cury and others taking a meaningful share.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has a market with this exact title. Snapshots I found from earlier in 2026 priced "Yes" at about 10-13%. I could not get a timestamped price close to 2026-09-26 because the aggregator page would not load. [SimpleFunctions mirror](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61)
- Kalshi has a related market, KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04 ("Will anyone win outright in the first round..."). I could not find a current price. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04), [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/odds/will-anyone-win-outright-in-the-brazil-presidential-election/6965)
- I found no formal expert or model forecast of a first-round win.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The last week of the campaign (Sept 26 to Oct 3): final TV debates, and final Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls, usually published the day before the vote. Watch for any candidate getting close to 50% of valid votes.
- Tactical voting: supporters of minor candidates (Cury, Caiado, Zema, Santos) switching to a front-runner at the last minute could push that front-runner up. Their combined share in early September was about 16%.
- Election day is 2026-10-04. The TSE usually publishes near-complete results the same night, so the question should be settled long before the 2027-06-30 deadline.

Sources: [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/quaest-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-36-flavio-29-e-cury-8/), [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html), [Harvard TagTeam](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content), [CBC](https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6603351), [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61), [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/odds/will-anyone-win-outright-in-the-brazil-presidential-election/6965)

2 Lula polled near 50% of valid votes and still finished at 48.4%, and polls underestimated the right.
  - Earlier polls (January Quaest, March Datafolha) were consistent with this picture.
- **For Yes:**
  - Late tactical consolidation of minor-candidate voters (about 16% combined) could lift Lula a few points.
  - Earlier Polymarket prices were 10-13%, though those reflect older information.
  - I found no polls from Sept 8 to 26, so there is some uncertainty about late movement.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** Final polls show Lula at about 44% of valid votes and Flávio at about 36%. Cury and the others hold 10-15%. Lula leads on Oct 4 but goes to a runoff on Oct 25.
- **Yes:** A late collapse of Cury and the centrist candidates, combined with a "vote útil" push to end it in one round, lifts Lula above 50% of valid votes. This would need roughly a 6-8 point gain in valid-vote share within a month, which has no precedent in recent cycles.

(f) **Adjustment.** I start from the modern base rate of about 7% and the market anchor of about 10-13%. That anchor is stale and has no confirmed price near the cutoff. The September polling puts the leader roughly 5-8 points of valid votes short, and a solid second candidate is near 30%. Historical polling error has gone against Lula in this exact situation. I therefore move down to about 4%. I don't go lower because there is a week of campaigning left, the late-September polls are missing, and polling error is plausible.

Probability: 4%

- Minor candidates (Cury, Caiado, Zema, Santos) held about 16% combined in early September, and tactical consolidation could happen late.
  - Polymarket priced Yes at 10-13% earlier in 2026.
- For No:
  - Quaest on 2026-09-07: Lula 36%, Flávio 29%, Cury 8%. That puts Lula at roughly 44-45% of valid votes.
  - Datafolha in March 2026 had a runoff technical tie (46-43), so the race is polarized and competitive.
  - In 2022, Lula polled near or above 50% of valid votes and still got only 48.4%, because polls underestimated the right.
  - Flávio's base at about 29-30% caps Lula's ceiling.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: The race stays polarized. Cury and the other minor candidates keep about 10-15%, Lula finishes around 44-47% of valid votes and Flávio around 37-40%, and a runoff follows on October 25.
- Yes: The minor candidates' supporters collapse toward Lula as a "decide it now" vote, a late scandal or event hurts Flávio, and Lula gains about 6 points of valid share in the last weeks to clear 50%.

(f) **From base rate to final probability.** I start from the 0-of-6 recent record and a broad historical rate of about 20%. I then move down sharply because the current leader is about 5-6 points of valid share short of 50% with a week to go. That gap is larger than 2022's, when he still fell short. Earlier market prices of 10-13% were set with less information and a less settled field. I allow a little for poll error and late consolidation, which puts me at about 4%.

Probability: 4%

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes: Lula has led every poll. In 2022 he reached 48.4% of valid votes, close to the threshold. Late tactical voting by supporters of minor candidates (about 16% combined) could consolidate behind a front-runner.
- For No:
  - In the Quaest poll of 2026-09-07, Lula had 36% of total votes against Flávio's 29%.
  - Cury holds about 8%, which drains share away from the front-runners.
  - In the Datafolha runoff simulation of 2026-03, the two were technically tied, so this is a polarized two-way race.
  - In 2022, polls overstated Lula's first-round share.
  - Polymarket priced Yes at about 10-13% earlier in 2026, before the field fragmented further.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No (most likely): Lula finishes around 43-46% of valid votes, Flávio around 37-40%, and both advance to a runoff on Oct 25.
- Yes: In the final week the minor candidates collapse, voters swing hard toward Lula to "settle it in the first round" (as he campaigned for in 2022), and polls understate him. He edges past 50%.

**(f) Moving to a final probability.**
- I start from a historical base of about 20% and cut it sharply because current polls put the leader 5-8 points short of the threshold one week out, with a strong second candidate.
- I also move below the older market price of 10-13%, since September polling shows no consolidation toward 50%.
- I keep some tail probability for late swings and polling error, which the 2022 result shows can be several points.

Probability: 4%
